evidence.claim: Census reported the 2022 Supplemental Poverty Measure rose to 12.4 percent, child SPM poverty more than doubled from 5.2 percent to 12.4 percent, and Social Security remained the largest anti-poverty program.
evidence.title: Poverty in the United States: 2022
evidence.excerpt: Census reported the 2022 Supplemental Poverty Measure rose to 12.4 percent, child SPM poverty more than doubled from 5.2 percent to 12.4 percent, and Social Security remained the largest anti-poverty program.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 poverty statistics with clear program decomposition.
evidence.period_fit: Directly measures target-year household hardship and safety-net effects.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broad Biden-term outcome, but much of the change reflects expiration of temporary pandemic relief rather than a new presidential choice in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The report shows strong safety-net effects even as poverty rose after pandemic aid expired.

evidence.claim: CDC reported the maternal mortality rate fell to 22.3 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2022, but Black women still had a rate of 49.5 compared with 19.0 for White women.
evidence.title: Maternal Mortality Rates in the United States, 2022
evidence.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
evidence.excerpt: CDC reported the maternal mortality rate fell to 22.3 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2022, but Black women still had a rate of 49.5 compared with 19.0 for White women.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national vital-statistics report with direct 2022 rates and disparities.
evidence.period_fit: Directly measures the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broader national outcome under Biden; not solely attributable to the president because maternity outcomes depend on health systems, states, and long-run inequities.
contrary_evidence: The racial disparity remained severe despite the year-to-year improvement.

evidence.claim: Census reported that expanded school meal eligibility and related pandemic-era policies were associated with declining food insecurity in households with children, including the use of P-EBT and free-meal flexibilities.
evidence.title: National School Lunch Program Still Important Part of Safety Net
evidence.excerpt: Census reported that expanded school meal eligibility and related pandemic-era policies were associated with declining food insecurity in households with children, including the use of P-EBT and free-meal flexibilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary survey-based analysis with explicit discussion of the policy channel.
evidence.period_fit: Measures policy effects that carried into the Biden period and framed 2022 safety-net conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited and pandemic-era, but the policy environment was still being maintained and extended under Biden.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes improving economic circumstances contributed, so not all change was policy-driven.

evidence.claim: USDA announced an additional $943 million for schools to buy food for meal programs in school year 2022-23 and said the Keep Kids Fed Act added temporary reimbursements and flexibilities for child nutrition providers.
evidence.title: Biden Administration Takes Additional Steps to Strengthen Child Nutrition Programs
evidence.excerpt: USDA announced an additional $943 million for schools to buy food for meal programs in school year 2022-23 and said the Keep Kids Fed Act added temporary reimbursements and flexibilities for child nutrition providers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 implementation announcement with specific funding and program details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration policy implementation through USDA, though Congress also mattered for the statute.
contrary_evidence: Funding does not by itself prove better nutritional outcomes.

evidence.claim: USDA said it extended WIC formula flexibility through the end of December 2022, covered the added cost of non-contract formula, and said nearly all state agencies had applicable waivers in place.
evidence.title: USDA Extends Flexibility that’s Helping Manufacturers, States get Formula to WIC Families
evidence.excerpt: USDA said it extended WIC formula flexibility through the end of December 2022, covered the added cost of non-contract formula, and said nearly all state agencies had applicable waivers in place.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous implementation record with clear program terms.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year response to the infant-formula shortage.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration crisis response through USDA and WIC administration.
contrary_evidence: This was a crisis mitigation measure, not a durable solution to formula market concentration.

evidence.claim: KFF reported 14.5 million people signed up for ACA Marketplace coverage for 2022, a 21 percent increase, and linked the rise to expanded ARPA subsidies and Biden administration outreach.
evidence.title: Marketplace Sign-ups Increased by 21% in 2022
evidence.excerpt: KFF reported 14.5 million people signed up for ACA Marketplace coverage for 2022, a 21 percent increase, and linked the rise to expanded ARPA subsidies and Biden administration outreach.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Strong independent policy research, though still an analytical summary rather than a direct administrative record.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 coverage year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Biden-era policy and outreach, with enrollment also shaped by market conditions and state exchanges.
contrary_evidence: Enrollment alone does not prove that coverage quality or affordability was uniform.

evidence.claim: CMS said Medicaid and CHIP together cover 51 percent of U.S. children and youth and issued guidance to expand children's behavioral health care, including school-based services and EPSDT mental-health coverage.
evidence.title: As American Families Prepare for Back-to-School, Biden-Harris Administration Strengthens Access to High-Quality, Comprehensive Health Care for Children
evidence.excerpt: CMS said Medicaid and CHIP together cover 51 percent of U.S. children and youth and issued guidance to expand children's behavioral health care, including school-based services and EPSDT mental-health coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct agency guidance with a clear coverage and service-delivery claim.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration policy through HHS/CMS, though implementation depends on states and providers.
contrary_evidence: Coverage share is inherited baseline as well as policy achievement.

evidence.claim: CMS said the new Medicaid mobile crisis intervention option gives people in crisis a qualified health professional as the first point of care, can avoid unnecessary emergency-room use and hospitalizations, and is supported by three years of additional federal funding.
evidence.title: New Medicaid Option Promotes Enhanced Mental Health, Substance Use Crisis Care
evidence.excerpt: CMS said the new Medicaid mobile crisis intervention option gives people in crisis a qualified health professional as the first point of care, can avoid unnecessary emergency-room use and hospitalizations, and is supported by three years of additional federal funding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct agency announcement with concrete service-design language.
evidence.period_fit: Implemented and expanded into the 2022 target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration crisis-care policy under ARPA authority.
contrary_evidence: The program is an option for states, not a nationwide guarantee of access.

evidence.claim: KFF reported that Medicaid enrollment reached 89.4 million by June 2022, an increase of 25.6 percent since February 2020, and said the continuous-enrollment requirement prevented coverage loss and churn.
evidence.title: Medicaid Enrollment & Spending Growth: FY 2022 & 2023
evidence.excerpt: KFF reported that Medicaid enrollment reached 89.4 million by June 2022, an increase of 25.6 percent since February 2020, and said the continuous-enrollment requirement prevented coverage loss and churn.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent health-policy analysis using state survey data and enrollment totals.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 coverage conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Biden-era pandemic coverage policy, though the program was created under FFCRA and depends on state administration.
contrary_evidence: The same mechanism creates a later unwinding problem when the emergency ends.

evidence.claim: HUD announced a $365 million package including $322 million for coordinated approaches to unsheltered homelessness and $43 million for about 4,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers, aimed at linking vulnerable people to housing and supportive services.
evidence.title: Biden Administration Announces First-Ever Funding Opportunity for Coordinated Approaches to Address Unsheltered Homelessness, Including Resources for Rural Communities
evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
evidence.excerpt: HUD announced a $365 million package including $322 million for coordinated approaches to unsheltered homelessness and $43 million for about 4,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers, aimed at linking vulnerable people to housing and supportive services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct agency announcement with amounts, beneficiaries, and policy purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration housing policy through HUD; Congress and local partners also matter for implementation.
contrary_evidence: Announcements do not by themselves prove durable housing exits or reduced homelessness everywhere.

evidence.claim: HUD awarded more than 19,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers and said emergency rental assistance improved housing stability for over 6 million unique households, including 700,000 HUD-assisted households.
evidence.title: FACT SHEET: HUD Awards More Than 19,000 New Housing Choice Vouchers in Most Expansive Allocation of Flexible Rental Assistance in 20 Years
evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
evidence.excerpt: HUD awarded more than 19,000 new Housing Choice Vouchers and said emergency rental assistance improved housing stability for over 6 million unique households, including 700,000 HUD-assisted households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct federal housing-program announcement with quantified scale and beneficiary description.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration housing policy through HUD and the FY 2022 budget context.
contrary_evidence: Voucher allocations are not the same as successful long-term placement or affordability in all markets.

evidence.claim: AP reported that Biden invoked the Defense Production Act to speed infant-formula production and authorized flights to import supply from overseas.
evidence.title: Biden invokes Defense Production Act to alleviate baby formula shortage
evidence.excerpt: AP reported that Biden invoked the Defense Production Act to speed infant-formula production and authorized flights to import supply from overseas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous AP reporting via a major outlet; strong for action and timing, though not a primary record.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year during the formula shortage crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden crisis response to a domestic shortage affecting infants and low-income families.
contrary_evidence: This was a mitigation response to a shortage the administration did not create.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the nationwide infant-formula shortage prompted temporary U.S. permission for foreign imports while the government reached a deal with Abbott to resume production at its Michigan plant.
evidence.title: Baby formula crunch in U.S. forces scramble to boost supplies
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the nationwide infant-formula shortage prompted temporary U.S. permission for foreign imports while the government reached a deal with Abbott to resume production at its Michigan plant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on crisis response, with some dissemination through a syndicator.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration crisis management, though the underlying shortage was driven by the Abbott plant shutdown and market concentration.
contrary_evidence: Import permissions are crisis mitigation rather than structural reform.

evidence.claim: Urban Institute said households earning median incomes or less could afford only 20 percent of homes for sale in late 2022, down from about half in 2016, underscoring the housing affordability crisis facing ordinary households.
evidence.title: Eighty Percent of Homes on the Market Aren’t Affordable for Households Earning Median Incomes or Less
evidence.excerpt: Urban Institute said households earning median incomes or less could afford only 20 percent of homes for sale in late 2022, down from about half in 2016, underscoring the housing affordability crisis facing ordinary households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent quantitative analysis, though not a direct policy-evaluation study of Biden actions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly describes target-year market conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly context and inherited market conditions rather than direct Biden control.
contrary_evidence: The article does not isolate Biden-specific causation.

evidence.claim: Brookings said Biden’s student debt forgiveness was intended to target low- and middle-income borrowers, especially Black borrowers, borrowers without a degree, and people in default.
evidence.title: Does Biden’s student debt forgiveness achieve his stated goals?
evidence.excerpt: Brookings said Biden’s student debt forgiveness was intended to target low- and middle-income borrowers, especially Black borrowers, borrowers without a degree, and people in default.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent expert analysis tied directly to the announced Biden policy, though still evaluative.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden policy choice and public framing.
contrary_evidence: The piece questions how well the policy actually targeted the intended groups.

evidence.claim: Brookings found Black households with student debt carry more debt and that debt cancellation would disproportionately help wealth-poor Black households by shifting wealth up the distribution and narrowing wealth gaps at lower percentiles.
evidence.title: Student loans, the racial wealth divide, and why we need full student debt cancellation
evidence.excerpt: Brookings found Black households with student debt carry more debt and that debt cancellation would disproportionately help wealth-poor Black households by shifting wealth up the distribution and narrowing wealth gaps at lower percentiles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent distributional analysis with concrete wealth findings, though not a 2022 outcome study.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 analysis that explains why Biden-era debt relief would matter for equity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Biden because it underpins his 2022 student-debt policy choices.
contrary_evidence: It is model-based and does not prove realized 2022 gains.

evidence.claim: Brookings said the pandemic worsened the higher-education access crisis and that marginalized students with less broadband and devices were disproportionately vulnerable to learning loss.
evidence.title: Whose learning counts? State actions to value skills from outside the classroom
evidence.excerpt: Brookings said the pandemic worsened the higher-education access crisis and that marginalized students with less broadband and devices were disproportionately vulnerable to learning loss.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent education-policy analysis, useful for equity context but not a direct performance evaluation.
evidence.period_fit: Describes conditions affecting the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited and structural context rather than a direct Biden decision.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show a specific Biden intervention in 2022.

evidence.claim: HRSA said Biden’s national mental-health strategy would expand the supply, diversity, and cultural competence of the mental-health and substance-use workforce, increase community health workers and peers, and expand rural treatment and community health centers.
evidence.title: Statement of HRSA Administrator on President's National Mental Health Strategy
evidence.excerpt: HRSA said Biden’s national mental-health strategy would expand the supply, diversity, and cultural competence of the mental-health and substance-use workforce, increase community health workers and peers, and expand rural treatment and community health centers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct implementation statement from the responsible federal agency with concrete program actions.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Biden-administration policy direction through HRSA and HHS.
contrary_evidence: Workforce expansion is necessary but does not by itself solve access gaps.

evidence.claim: HRSA’s RMOMS program was designed to improve access to and continuity of maternal and obstetrics care in rural communities and to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes through sustainable regional networks.
evidence.title: Rural Maternity and Obstetrics Management Strategies Program
evidence.excerpt: HRSA’s RMOMS program was designed to improve access to and continuity of maternal and obstetrics care in rural communities and to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes through sustainable regional networks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct grant-program notice with explicit goals and implementation design.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year program design and funding opportunity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Biden-administration health access policy through HRSA, though grant uptake depends on applicants and local providers.
contrary_evidence: A funding opportunity is not the same as realized service expansion.

evidence.claim: Census reported that child poverty measured by the Supplemental Poverty Measure fell to a record low 5.2% in 2021 and said the expanded Child Tax Credit materially contributed to the decline.
evidence.title: Expansions to Child Tax Credit Contributed to 46% Decline in Child Poverty Since 2020
evidence.excerpt: Census reported that child poverty measured by the Supplemental Poverty Measure fell to a record low 5.2% in 2021 and said the expanded Child Tax Credit materially contributed to the decline.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary federal statistical release with precise target-period outcome data and explicit policy attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to Biden-era social-welfare effects in the 2021-2022 policy window; retrospective to 2021 but published in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong: the effect is tied to ARPA/CTC expansions advanced under Biden and implemented by federal agencies.
contrary_evidence: Official poverty fell only 0.7 percentage points.
Durability was limited because the expansion later expired.

evidence.claim: Brookings noted that the American Rescue Plan Child Tax Credit expansion had ended, leaving nearly 19 million of the poorest children with no or only a partial credit and showing the gains were not durable without extension.
evidence.title: Next steps on the Child Tax Credit
evidence.excerpt: Brookings noted that the American Rescue Plan Child Tax Credit expansion had ended, leaving nearly 19 million of the poorest children with no or only a partial credit and showing the gains were not durable without extension.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent policy analysis that directly evaluates the distributional durability of the 2021-2022 child-welfare gains.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 analysis of the post-expansion welfare environment; relevant as a durability caveat for target-year gains.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the policy design and lapse under Biden-era conditions, but this source is mainly a follow-on durability critique rather than a fresh 2022 delivery action.
contrary_evidence: The same Brookings line acknowledges the earlier ARPA expansion sharply reduced child poverty.
This is a follow-on critique, not a contemporaneous delivery record.

evidence.claim: CMS said 14.5 million people signed up for 2022 Marketplace coverage and that 5.8 million people newly gained coverage since the start of the Biden-Harris Administration.
evidence.title: Biden-Harris Administration Announces 14.5 Million Americans Signed Up for Affordable Health Care During Historic Open Enrollment Period
evidence.excerpt: CMS said 14.5 million people signed up for 2022 Marketplace coverage and that 5.8 million people newly gained coverage since the start of the Biden-Harris Administration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary agency release with a dated enrollment outcome and explicit administration attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 coverage outcome, though the enrollment season spans late 2021 into early 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but mediated through ACA subsidies and CMS outreach; Biden publicly framed the action and the underlying subsidies.
contrary_evidence: Enrollment gains were partly subsidy-driven rather than a pure delivery metric.
The release is enrollment, not health outcome, data.

evidence.claim: CMS said four out of five Marketplace customers could find plans for $10 or less per month after tax credits during the 2022 open-enrollment period.
evidence.title: Biden-Harris Administration Launches 10th Year of Marketplace Open Enrollment with Four Out of Five Customers Eligible for Coverage at $10 or Less, Thanks to Subsidies
evidence.excerpt: CMS said four out of five Marketplace customers could find plans for $10 or less per month after tax credits during the 2022 open-enrollment period.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official statement with a concrete affordability metric and policy linkage to Biden-signed subsidies.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 open-enrollment evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Biden-backed ACA/IRA subsidy policy and CMS implementation, not solely to the president personally.
contrary_evidence: This is premium affordability, not total out-of-pocket cost.
Actual plan uptake still depends on consumer choice and state-marketplace participation.

evidence.claim: USICH said the 2022 Point-in-Time Count showed an 11% decline in veteran homelessness since early 2020, the biggest drop in more than five years.
evidence.title: New Data Shows 11% Decline in Veteran Homelessness Since 2020—the Biggest Drop in 5+ Years
evidence.publisher: United States Interagency Council on Homelessness
evidence.excerpt: USICH said the 2022 Point-in-Time Count showed an 11% decline in veteran homelessness since early 2020, the biggest drop in more than five years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary interagency release with a quantified target-year outcome and clear attribution chain.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 outcome on a vulnerable population.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed by USICH to the Biden-era VA/HUD/USICH effort, though the result also reflects local systems and the pandemic baseline.
contrary_evidence: This covers veterans only, not homelessness overall.
The count was a two-year interval because the 2021 count was incomplete.

evidence.claim: GAO said the Emergency Rental Assistance program helped prevent evictions and housing instability, while also noting oversight weaknesses.
evidence.title: Emergency Rental Assistance Helped Prevent Evictions, But Oversight of Payments Was Limited
evidence.excerpt: GAO said the Emergency Rental Assistance program helped prevent evictions and housing instability, while also noting oversight weaknesses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent federal oversight source that directly addresses both benefit and implementation limits.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 housing-stability evidence, using the pandemic-response program still active under Biden.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly indirect because the program was congressionally funded and administered through Treasury, but the Biden administration was responsible for implementation and oversight choices.
contrary_evidence: GAO also warned about payment oversight and data limitations.
This is pandemic-response aid rather than a Biden-created program from scratch.

evidence.claim: Biden launched the student-loan relief application, said it was simple and available in English and Spanish, and said more than 40 million Americans could benefit, with about 90% of the benefit going to people making under $75,000.
evidence.title: Remarks on the Federal Student Loan Debt Relief Program and an Exchange With Reporters
evidence.excerpt: Biden launched the student-loan relief application, said it was simple and available in English and Spanish, and said more than 40 million Americans could benefit, with about 90% of the benefit going to people making under $75,000.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential remarks with concrete distributional claims and a clear implementation milestone.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 policy launch and rollout.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action and messaging, though legal authority and agency execution were necessary for delivery.
contrary_evidence: The program was still at the application stage in 2022.
Implementation and legal durability were contested.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 command-and-control and safeguards evidence is thinner than the public nuclear rhetoric and treaty-posture record.
The strongest crisis evidence is mostly speeches and reported private warnings rather than a declassified operational de-escalation record.
Direct 2022 documentary evidence on private diplomacy, ceasefire channels, and partner-use limits remains thinner than the public sanctions and aid record.
National-level evidence on protest policing, retaliation for dissent, and the federal government's leverage over local police remains thinner than the anti-hate and gun-safety record.
Border-enforcement attribution is still mixed because a large share of the harmful conduct sits in inherited systems and sub-agency action.
Direct evidence on state-level election administration, intimidation, and coercive presidential leverage against opponents is still limited.
Household distribution by race, region, and income tier is thinner than the macro and legislative record.
The causal split between Biden-era policy, global shocks, and Federal Reserve tightening remains mixed.
Child care, disability services, and elder-care evidence is still thin compared with health, housing, food, and crisis-response coverage.
The housing record is strong on funding and program design but weaker on realized rent-burden and eviction-prevention outcomes in 2022.
Direct personal-nexus evidence on recusal, ethics waivers, family-business benefit, or obstruction of scrutiny remains thin.
The clearest negative pattern is repeated factual exaggeration in speeches, but the record lacks equally direct correction or retraction evidence.
Independent project-level verification of 2022 execution for CHIPS, IRA, and infrastructure remains thinner than the policy-architecture record.
Community-level outcomes for specific groups and regions are still not well verified in the package.
